subject: Business Models
title: Geographic Density
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Geographic Density.

hook.text: Uber launched city by city, not country by country. Density in one city beats thin coverage everywhere.

buildup.text: Location-based marketplaces need geographic density. A driver 30 minutes away is useless.

discovery.text: DoorDash won by saturating suburbs first—areas Uber Eats ignored while chasing big cities.

twist.text: High density in one zip code can be more profitable than thin coverage across 50 cities.

climax.text: Geographic focus creates local network effects that compound before expansion even begins.

punchline.text: Win one city completely before expanding to the next. Density beats breadth.

quiz.question: Why did DoorDash focus on suburbs first?

details.summary: Geographic density measures the concentration of marketplace supply and demand within a specific area. For location-dependent services like ride-sharing, food delivery, and home repair.
details.whyItMatters: Many marketplace failures result from spreading too thin across too many geographies. Dense liquidity in one city generates a much better experience than sparse coverage across ten cities..
takeaways: Location-dependent marketplaces need dense supply within each geographic market
Sparse geographic coverage creates poor experiences that prevent network effects
Launching in a single dense market builds a template for controlled geographic expansion

faq.question: Why is geographic density more important than total market size?
faq.answer: A marketplace with 1,000 providers in one city delivers fast, reliable service. The same 1,000 providers spread across 50 cities means 20 per city, resulting in long wait times and poor selection. Users judge marketplace quality by their local experience, not the platform's total size.

faq.question: How do marketplaces expand geographically while maintaining density?
faq.answer: They launch in one market, achieve density and profitability, then expand to similar adjacent markets one at a time. Each new market gets focused investment until it reaches critical density..
